findings.problem: This class is new in u10's trail; r1 and r2 missed it, because we tested orders, doublets and numbers, not person and vowel forms. a1.1-u03 r3-F01 found it after our r2 and counted eight u10 items, and a1.1-u08 r3-F03 confirmed it. check.js calls a one-letter difference a typo unless the last letter changes. Three kinds of error change an inner letter and so come back TYPO: the stem umlaut (fahrt/fährt, fahre/fähre), the stem vowel of treffen (trefft/trifft), and the person endings -st/-t (nimmst/nimmt, kommst/kommt, fährst/fährt). ItemView gives one retry and then logs the same answer as correct. In u10 this hits the whole of LS2's point, g.vokalwechsel. Its rule card says exactly „a → ä … Bei ich, wir, ihr und sie/Sie bleibt der Vokal“, yet the missing umlaut („fahrst“) and the wrongly added one („fähre“) both pass. It hits both scored Check items on verbs (c01, c03). It hits ls2-p10 hardest: the player prefills an error correction with its quoted sentence, so a learner who presses „Prüfen“ twice without touching „Du fahrst am Abend zurück.“ has the item logged as correct. On this point the grader is inverted: a genuine slip such as the transposition „färht“ is WRONG, while the target error „fahrt“ is a TYPO. We checked every other typed item: the -in items are safe (the ending changes the last letter), and so are the separable-verb corrections (a two-token change). A grader that accepts the error an item exists to remove is a gate hole that lets a finding class through (§9.4 MAJOR).
